For the collector

LEGO Icons Concorde

An evening project that becomes a permanent part of their aviation corner. A strong choice for someone who loves airliners as much as flying them.

Before you buy: Allow a long display shelf: the finished model measures 41.5 inches. Ages 18+.

$199.99LEGO ↗
A useful little extra

Flight Gear Aviator’s Light

A compact light with separate red and white controls. It makes sense for the person who likes keeping small, useful tools in their flight bag.

Before you buy: Ask what light they already carry; this is an accessory, not a replacement for required equipment.

$29.95Sporty’s ↗
A milestone keepsake

Cessna 172 Skyhawk model

The best model is often the aircraft with a story behind it. This mahogany Skyhawk is especially thoughtful for someone who learned to fly a Cessna 172.

Before you buy: Confirm their aircraft type. A 172 and a 182 are different airplanes, even if they look similar.

$249.00Pilot Mall ↗
Under $25

SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

Before you buy: Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.

$24.50Pilot Mall ↗
For their next flight

Flight Gear Stealth Bag

A flight bag is a gift they can use beyond the holidays. This compact backpack-style option is worth a look when their current setup is an overflowing ordinary bag.

Before you buy: Compare the listed dimensions with their headset, tablet and usual load before choosing.

$79.95Sporty’s ↗
A little holiday aviation

Blue Angels jet ornament

A small nod to a favorite airshow team. Add it to a larger gift, or make it the start of an aviation ornament tradition.

Before you buy: Best for a Blue Angels fan; a favorite aircraft or team makes a small gift feel personal.

$17.99Pilot Mall ↗
For the organized pilot

Flight Gear rotating kneeboard

A practical way to keep a compatible iPad in reach. It is most useful when you already know the pilot wants a kneeboard rather than a mounted tablet.

Before you buy: Confirm the exact iPad model, case and preferred cockpit setup with the retailer.

$22.95Sporty’s ↗
For a first lesson

ASA pilot logbook

An affordable way to mark the start of flight training. Pair it with a note about the journey ahead, rather than filling in any flight-record pages yourself.

Before you buy: Check with their instructor first: they may already have a logbook or use a different format.

$9.49Pilot Mall ↗
Off-duty aviation

Cessna patch trucker cap

A casual option for the Cessna enthusiast who already owns the flight gear they need. The navy-and-scarlet color scheme makes it easy to wear away from the airport.

Before you buy: Confirm they like caps and Cessna; a familiar logo is more personal than a random airplane.

$34.99Pilot Mall ↗
Wear their favorite airplane

Cessna 182 Skylane tee

A good match for someone with a connection to the Skylane. Aircraft-specific clothing works best when the reference is meaningful to the person receiving it.

Before you buy: Choose the right size and check the seller’s return policy before ordering.

$29.99Pilot Mall ↗
A small travel upgrade

Pro Crew luggage tag

A low-cost gift for a working pilot’s luggage. It is especially easy to combine with a card or another small item when you want something useful to unwrap.

Before you buy: A CREW tag is a bag accessory, not airport identification or an access credential.

$9.99Pilot Mall ↗
The choose-together gift

Bose A30 aviation headset

A serious equipment gift for someone who has specifically asked for an A30. Let the pilot choose the connection and configuration rather than making this an expensive surprise.

Before you buy: Confirm aircraft plug, power arrangement and fit. Listed price is for the linked configuration.

$1,299.00Pilot Mall ↗
For the upgrade wishlist

Lightspeed Zulu 3 headset

Another premium headset to consider when it is already on their wishlist. A gift contribution can be more thoughtful than guessing between competing headset preferences.

Before you buy: Choose the correct connection and have the recipient check fit and return terms.

$949.00Pilot Mall ↗
Let the pilot choose

Sporty’s email gift card

Useful when their wishlist gets technical—or the shipping window has closed. It lets the recipient choose the exact accessory, size or equipment version they need.

Before you buy: Check delivery timing and available values at checkout. Gift cards have their own redemption terms.

Before you check out

Four checks.
One better gift.

Read the full checklist ↗
  1. Find the personal connection. Their first airplane, favorite airshow, or an item they actually asked for.
  2. Check the fit. Aircraft plugs, tablet models, clothing sizes and shelf space all matter.
  3. Check the delivered total. Include tax and shipping, then read the delivery estimate and return terms.
  4. Keep technical gifts collaborative. For headsets and cockpit equipment, let the pilot choose the exact version.
